f.title: Perform signal detection and management at product-name and active-substance level
f.statement: Signal detection for biologicals should be specific to the product as well as the active substance, and all steps of signal management should be performed at the level of the product name as well as the active substance.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote:
Signal detection for biologicals should therefore be specific to the product, as well as the active

well as the active substance.

rows.review_note: Review: quote extended to the second sentence ("All steps of signal management should be performed at the level of the product name...") which the statement already contained. Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Seek a common root cause such as batch for any signal
f.statement: In case of a signal, any effort should be made to identify any common root cause such as batch.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: In case of a signal any effort should be made to identify any common root cause such as batch.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: statement wording aligned to the quote ("any effort"). Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Make signal processes sensitive to risks after manufacturing/quality changes and between batches
f.statement: Signal processes should be particularly sensitive to detect acute and serious new risks emerging after a change in the manufacturing process or quality of a biological, and important differences between batches of the same product, especially after a significant manufacturing change since the product name usually does not change.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Processes should be particularly sensitive to detect any acute and serious new risks that may emerge following a change in the manufacturing process or quality of a biological and important differences between batches of the same product (this is particularly important following a significant change to the manufacturing process given that the product name usually does not change).
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: survivor of duplicate 0100 (P.II.C.1.1.2 restates the same sensitivity duty for MAHs); B.4 kept as the fuller wording (product-name parenthetical). Double-check: quote opens 'Processes' (signal processes from the preceding sentence); actor inferred.

f.title: Identify important differences between reference products and biosimilars
f.statement: Important differences between reference products and biosimilars or related products should be identified during the product life-cycle based on available information.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management
f.applicability: Reference products, biosimilars and related products

rows.quote: Important differences between reference products and biosimilars or related products should be identified during the product(s) life-cycle based on the available information.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: survivor of duplicate 0101 (P.II.C.1.1.2, identical duty restated for MAHs). Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Monitor clinical consequences of emerging immunogenicity throughout the life-cycle
f.statement: Any clinical consequences of potential emerging immunogenicity (as a theoretical risk) should be monitored throughout the product life-cycle.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Any clinical consequences of potential emerging immunogenicity (as a theoretical risk) should be monitored throughout the product life-cycle.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: survivor of duplicate 0102 (P.II.C.1.1.2, identical quote restated for MAHs). Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Obtain product-specific actual usage data from all available sources
f.statement: MAHs should make every effort to obtain data on actual usage specific to a product and explore all methods and data sources to obtain reliable and updated information.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders should make every effort to obtain data on actual usage specific to a product (see P.II.B.3.) and explore all methods and data sources to obtain reliable and updated information.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: no change; overlaps 0067 (PSUR exposure section) but kept separate: signal-management context and adds exploring all methods and data sources. Double-check: partial overlap with 0067 (actual usage data); kept for the added duty to explore all methods and data sources.

f.title: Analyse denominator and ADR data for continuous signal detection
f.statement: Denominator data and suspected adverse reaction data should be analysed to support continuous signal detection, particularly to detect apparent changes in reporting rates or trends that could indicate new signals (particularly after manufacturing changes).
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Denominator data and data of suspected adverse reactions (see GVP Module IX) should be analysed to support continuous signal detection and particularly detection of any apparent changes in suspected adverse reaction reporting rates or trends that could indicate new signals (particularly following manufacturing changes).
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Specify increased monitoring or specific signal detection activities in the RMP
f.statement: Some active substances or products may be subject to increased frequency of data monitoring, and a significant manufacturing change may, case by case, justify specific signal detection activities; any such requirements should be specified in the risk management plan.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Some active substances or medicinal products may also be subject to an increased frequency of data monitoring and a significant change in the manufacturing process of a biological may, on a case-by-case basis, justify specific signal detection activities (see GVP Module IX). Any such requirements should be specified in the risk management plan (see P.II.B.1.1.3. and P.II.B.1.2.).
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: mixes descriptive 'may be subject'/'may justify' with the 'should be specified' duty.

f.title: Consult disproportionality and observed-vs-expected methods as needed
f.statement: Continuous disproportionality analysis and observed vs expected methods (GVP P.I, GVP Module IX Addendum I, ENCePP methodological guide) should also be consulted as needed.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Continuous disproportionality analysis and ‘observed vs expected’ methods (see GVP Considerations P.I., the GVP Module IX Addendum I and the ENCePP Guide on Methodological Standards in Pharmacoepidemiology 18) should also be consulted as needed.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'consulted as needed' is soft wording; actor inferred.

f.title: Evaluate signals against batch-specific exposure data
f.statement: Any signal should be evaluated in the context of batch-specific exposure data, including numbers/codes of delivered or sold batches, their size and the regions or countries where they were delivered.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Any signal should be evaluated in the context of batch-specific exposure data, including numbers/codes of delivered or sold batches, their size and the regions or countries where the respective batches have been delivered.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Judge case by case whether a new signal is product-specific or substance-wide
f.statement: For new signals, case-by-case judgements are required on whether the signal may apply to the concerned product or to all products with the same active substance.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities
rows.quote: For new signals, case-by-case judgements are required on whether or not the signal may apply to the concerned product or to all products with the same active substance.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: level Mandatory -> Recommended: "case-by-case judgements are required" describes the evaluation approach, no legal duty or "shall"/"must". Double-check: level Recommended -> Mandatory for consistency (GVP V/VII convention: 'is required'/'requires' = Mandatory); 'judgements are required' describes an evaluation approach and the actor (MAHs and authorities) is inferred.

f.title: Regulatory action may extend to reference product or biosimilar on a precautionary basis
f.statement: On a precautionary basis, inadequate evidence on the specificity of a signal detected for a biosimilar or related product may justify regulatory action for the reference product, and vice versa.
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management
f.applicability: Reference products, biosimilars and related products

rows.quote: However, on a precautionary basis, inadequate evidence on the specificity of a signal detected for a biosimilar or related product may justify application of a regulatory action to the reference product, and vice versa.
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: authority-actor row kept: precautionary regulatory action may reach the reference product or biosimilar, which shapes the MAH's signal assessment across same-INN products. Double-check: authority-actor row; Permitted precautionary regulatory action.

f.title: Fully investigate new risks with suspected immunogenic aetiology
f.statement: Any new clinical risk suspected to have an immunogenic aetiology should be fully investigated to determine whether it is specific to a product name or batch and to evaluate its potential root cause, to determine the potential for risk minimisation or elimination (e.g. improved assays, manufacturing steps).
f.clause: P.II.B.4. Signal management

rows.quote: Any new clinical risk suspected to have an immunogenic aetiology should be fully investigated to determine whether the risk is specific to a product name or batch and evaluate its potential root cause in order to determine the potential for risk minimisation or elimination (e.g. improved assays, manufacturing steps).
rows.location: P.II.B.4. Signal management
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement; survivor of duplicate 0037 (P.II.B.1.1.3.2 stated the same full exploration and root-cause duty for new risks of immunogenic aetiology), removed.

f.title: Biologicals authorised after 1 January 2011 are subject to additional monitoring
f.statement: Biologicals authorised after 1 January 2011 shall be included in the list of medicinal products subject to additional monitoring.
f.clause: P.II.B.5. Additional monitoring
f.applicability: Biologicals authorised after 1 January 2011

rows.quote: Biologicals authorised after 1 January 2011 shall be included in the list of medicinal products that are subject to additional monitoring [REG Art 23(1)(b)].
rows.location: P.II.B.5. Additional monitoring
rows.review_note: Review: authority/list row kept: inclusion in the additional monitoring list triggers the MAH Module X duties (0105). Double-check: authority/list row (Agency's additional monitoring list); legal 'shall'.

f.title: Remove biologicals from additional monitoring list five years after Union reference date
f.statement: Biologicals under the mandatory scope shall be removed from the additional monitoring list five years after the Union reference date, unless the period of additional monitoring is extended.
f.clause: P.II.B.5. Additional monitoring

rows.deadline: Five years after the Union reference date, unless the additional monitoring period is extended
rows.quote: They shall be removed from the list under the mandatory scope five years after the Union reference date unless the period of additional monitoring is extended [REG Art 23(3)].
rows.location: P.II.B.5. Additional monitoring
rows.review_note: Review: kept: the end of mandatory-scope additional monitoring changes the MAH's Module X obligations. Double-check: authority/list row; legal 'shall', deadline clear.

f.title: Be aware of and address specific concerns about biologicals
f.statement: There should be awareness of the specific concerns that patients and healthcare professionals frequently have about biologicals, so that they can be addressed.
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.quote: There should be awareness of specific concerns that patients and healthcare professionals frequently have in relation to biologicals, so that they can be addressed.
rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified; 'There should be awareness' is vague.

f.title: Communicate manufacturing, active substance and excipient information to patients and HCPs
f.statement: Information on the manufacturing process and its variability, the active substance and its mode of action, and the excipients and possible residues should be communicated to patients and healthcare professionals for their good understanding.
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.quote: Hence, information on the manufacturing process and its variability, the active substance and its mode of action as well as the excipients and possible residues should be communicated to patients and health care professionals for their good understanding.
rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified.

f.title: Fulfil immunogenicity information needs consistently in communications
f.statement: Immunogenicity is a specific source of concern for biologicals, resulting in information needs to be fulfilled consistently (P.II.B.6 safety communication).
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.quote:
Immunogenicity is a specific source of concerns for biologicals, resulting in information needs to be
fulfilled consistently.
rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: added missed expectation (P.II.B.6) that immunogenicity information needs be fulfilled consistently; wording is "to be fulfilled", treated as Recommended. Double-check: actor not specified; 'resulting in information needs to be fulfilled' is descriptive, not a modal verb, so the Recommended level is a judgement call; statement trimmed to the quote.

f.title: Address previous exposure to same or cross-immunogenic products in communications
f.statement: Issues around previous exposure to the same or cross-immunogenic products may also have to be addressed in communication documents.
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.quote: Issues around previous exposure to the same or cross-immunogenic products may also have to be addressed in communication documents.
rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified; 'may also have to be addressed' is ambiguous between Permitted and Recommended.

f.title: EMA biosimilar Q&A and EC consensus document may be used for explanations
f.statement: The EMA Questions and Answers on Biosimilar Medicines and the European Commission Consensus Information Document "What you need to know about biosimilar medicinal products" may be used as sources for explanations when drafting product-specific communication documents.
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
f.applicability: Biosimilars

rows.quote: The EMA Questions and Answers on Biosimilar Medicines (similar biological medicinal products)20, drawn up in consultation with patient and healthcare professional representatives, and the European Commission’s Consensus Information Document “What you need to know about biosimilar medicinal products”21 may be used as a source for explanations when drafting product-specific communication documents.
rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified.

f.title: RMP summary and comparability data may be used in communications

f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified.

f.title: Communicate that ADRs may arise even after previous good tolerance
f.statement: It should be communicated to patients and healthcare professionals that adverse reactions may arise even if a product was previously well tolerated (e.g. due to manufacturing variability or changes, or long-term or delayed-onset effects), and that reporting suspected adverse reactions even after long-term use or with unknown features is important.
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.quote: It should be communicated to patients and healthcare professionals that adverse reactions may arise even if a medicinal product has previously been well tolerated, e.g. due to a manufacturing variability or changes or long-term or delayed onset effects, and that reporting of suspected adverse reactions occurring even after long-term use or with unknown features is important.
rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified.

f.title: Emphasise providing product name and batch number when reporting ADRs
f.statement: Communication should emphasise the importance of providing the product name (or INN and name of the MAH) and batch number(s) when reporting suspected adverse reactions.
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified.

f.title: Communication may aim at avoiding storage, cold chain and administration errors
f.statement: Other specific safety communication objectives for biologicals may aim at avoiding errors in storage and handling, in particular cold chain requirements, and administration, which frequently requires specific medical devices.
f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.quote: Other specific safety communication objectives in relation to biologicals may aim at avoiding errors in storage and handling, in particular as regards cold chain requirements (see P.II.A.1.3.) and administration which frequently requires specific medical devices.

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified; 'objectives ... may aim at' is descriptive.

f.title: Consult patients and HCPs on draft communication documents

f.clause: P.II.B.6. Safety communication

rows.location: P.II.B.6. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor not specified.

f.title: Authorise biotechnology-derived products through the centralised procedure
f.statement: Medicinal products developed by one of the biotechnology processes listed in the Annex of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, or fulfilling any other criteria of the Annex, shall be authorised in the EU through the centralised procedure.

rows.quote: Medicinal products developed by means of one of the biotechnology processes listed in the Annex of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, or fulfilling any other criteria of the Annex, shall be authorised in the EU through the centralised authorisation procedure.

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves legal 'shall' and statement.

f.title: Applicant is responsible for submitting the RMP per GVP Module V and P.II.B.1.1

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves actor, responsibility and statement.

f.title: Include name and batch number(s) of the administered biological in ICSRs
f.statement: When reporting suspected adverse reactions, MAHs shall provide all available information on each individual case, including for biologicals the name and batch number(s) of the administered product.
f.clause: P.II.C.1.1.2. Reporting of adverse reactions and signal management

rows.quote: When reporting suspected adverse reactions, marketing authorisation holders shall provide all available information on each individual case, including, for biologicals, the name and batch number(s) of the administered product [IR Art 28(3)(h)].

f.title: Include batch delivery information in the PSUR where relevant
f.statement: Where relevant to interpreting safety data, including a new signal detected in the PSUR interval, MAHs should include in the PSUR a summary of relevant information on batches delivered during the reporting period: batch numbers, EU Member States and regions of delivery, batch sizes and any available information on number of batches delivered per country.
f.clause: P.II.C.1.1.3. Periodic safety update report (PSUR)

rows.quote: Where relevant to the interpretation of safety data, including a new safety signal that has been detected in the interval covered by the PSUR, marketing authorisation holders should include in the PSUR a summary of relevant information on the batches delivered during the PSUR reporting period, including batch numbers, countries (EU Member States) and regions where such batches have been delivered, size of the batches and any available information on the number of batches that were delivered per country.
rows.location: P.II.C.1.1.3. Periodic safety update report (PSUR)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves actor, modal and data items.

f.title: Provide assumptions used for batch calculations in the PSUR

f.clause: P.II.C.1.1.3. Periodic safety update report (PSUR)

rows.quote: All assumptions used for calculations should be provided.
rows.location: P.II.C.1.1.3. Periodic safety update report (PSUR)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote lacks lead-in (which calculations); context from the preceding PSUR batch sentence.

f.title: Perform GVP Module X activities for biologicals under additional monitoring
f.statement: For biologicals on the additional monitoring list under the mandatory or optional scope, the MAH is responsible for performing the activities described in GVP Module X.

f.applicability: Biologicals subject to additional monitoring

rows.quote: For biologicals included in the list of medicinal products subject to additional monitoring according to the mandatory or optional scope [REG Art 23 (1) and (1a)], it is the responsibility of the marketing authorisation holder to perform the activities described in GVP Module X.
rows.location: P.II.C.1.1.4. Additional monitoring
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves actor, responsibility and legal basis.

f.title: Consider safety communication throughout the biological life-cycle and follow P.II.C.2

rows.quote: Further to the guidance in P.II.B.6., safety communication is an important activity to be considered by the marketing authorisation holder throughout the life-cycle of biologicals, and P.II.C.2. should be followed for additional EU-specific guidance.
rows.location: P.II.C.1.1.5. Safety communication
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'important activity to be considered' mixed with 'should be followed' cross-reference; level partly a judgement call.

f.title: Member States ensure clear identification of biologicals in suspected ADR reports
f.statement: Member States shall ensure, through methods for collecting information and where necessary follow-up of reports, that all appropriate measures are taken to clearly identify any biological prescribed, dispensed or sold in their territory that is the subject of a suspected adverse reaction report, with due regard to the product name and batch number.

rows.quote: Member States shall ensure, through the methods for collecting information and where necessary through the follow-up of suspected adverse reaction reports, that all appropriate measures are taken to identify clearly any biological prescribed, dispensed or sold in their territory which is the subject of a suspected adverse reaction report, with due regard to the name of the medicinal product (as defined in DIR Art 1(20)], and the batch number [DIR Art 102(e)].
rows.location: P.II.C.1.2.2. Reporting of adverse reactions

f.title: Agree a traceability system with national competent authorities
f.statement: To fulfil this obligation, national competent authorities should agree with MAHs, where applicable, a system to ensure traceability of biologicals prescribed, dispensed or sold; inform healthcare professionals and patients of the need to provide the product name (brand/invented name or INN with MAH name) and batch number/code when reporting; and make this information available to assessors for signal detection and case evaluation.
f.clause: P.II.C.1.2.2. Reporting of adverse reactions
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Local PV interfaces; Safety intake & collection

rows.actor: National competent authorities (with marketing authorisation holders)
rows.quote: To fulfil this obligation, national competent authorities should agree with marketing authorisation holders, where applicable, a system to ensure the traceability of the biologicals that are prescribed, dispensed or sold, inform healthcare professionals and patients of the need to provide the product name (i.e. brand/invented name or, as appropriate, INN accompanied by the name of the marketing authorisation holder) and batch number/code when reporting a suspected adverse reaction and make this information available to assessors for signal detection and evaluation of individual case reports.
rows.location: P.II.C.1.2.2. Reporting of adverse reactions
rows.review_note: Review: authority-actor row kept: national competent authorities agree the traceability system with MAHs. Double-check: authority-led row (national competent authorities agree system with MAHs).

f.title: Agency provides MAHs support for product-level EudraVigilance monitoring
f.statement: For signal detection of biologicals, the Agency should provide rapporteurs, lead Member States and national competent authorities with eRMRs and other outputs at product rather than substance level, and provide MAHs with appropriate support for monitoring EudraVigilance at product level.
f.clause: P.II.C.1.3. European Medicines Agency

rows.quote: For signal detection of biologicals, the Agency should provide rapporteurs, lead Member States and national competent authorities with electronic reaction monitoring reports and other data outputs and statistical reports at the product level rather than at the substance level and provide marketing authorisation holders with appropriate support for the monitoring of the EudraVigilance database at the product level.
rows.location: P.II.C.1.3. European Medicines Agency
